ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: Figure 9 is a soil water balance chart, with the horizontal axis as January—December and the vertical axis as water amount (mm). In the figure there are two curves, “precipitation” and “water requirement,” and regions such as “water replenishment,” “water deficit,” and “water utilization” are marked. In the figure, from about April to November, the water requirement curve is higher than the precipitation curve most of the time, and there is an obvious “water deficit” region. Then reason: during cultivation, crop water demand mainly depends on the comparison between water requirement and natural precipitation. The figure shows that during a relatively long period, natural precipitation cannot meet water requirements, soil water supply is insufficient, and the main limiting factor is water shortage. Therefore, the problem that most needs to be solved for cultivation on this soil is irrigation.

raw_record.question_text: According to the soil water balance situation shown in Figure 9, <image1>, what is the problem that most needs to be solved for cultivation on this soil?

method.method_draft: 先描述图像：图9是土壤水分收支图，横轴为1—12月，纵轴为水量；图中有“降水量”和“水分需要量”等曲线。再推理：比较两条曲线，发现较长时期内水分需要量高于降水量，说明自然降水不能满足耕作需水，主要矛盾是缺水。因此该土壤耕作最需解决的问题是灌溉。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This route uses a month-by-month comparison of the two main curves, deriving the limiting factor from the repeated gap where demand is above precipitation. It is distinct from simply reading the named deficit zone because it treats the diagram as a water-balance graph and infers the management need from curve relationships.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the graph axes as monthly water amount in mm. Identify the curve labeled “降水量” and the curve labeled “水分需要量”, then note that from roughly spring to autumn, especially around 4–10月, water demand is generally higher than precipitation, forming a large deficit interval.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question wording “在该土壤上进行耕作最需解决的问题是什么” to frame the task as identifying the chief agricultural constraint from the water-balance diagram.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: For cultivation, when crop/soil water demand exceeds natural precipitation over the main growing period, the primary corrective measure is to supply water artificially, i.e. irrigation.

It is weakly distinct because it reaches the same single obvious management conclusion from labeled deficit evidence.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the labeled regions in the figure: “水分亏缺” occupies a broad central part of the year, and there is also “储存水的消耗”, showing that soil stored water is being used up before later recovery/利用. These labels visually indicate insufficient available water.

planner_metadata.knowledge_role: A broad labeled soil-water deficit and consumption of stored soil moisture mean that crops face drought stress; the direct agricultural measure to overcome soil moisture shortage is irrigation.
